original_value: AbstractWe provide a detailed study of the threshold model, where both conformist and anti-conformist agents coexist. Our study bears essentially on the convergence of the opinion dynamics in the society of agents, i.e., finding absorbing classes, cycles, etc. Also, we are interested in the existence of cascade effects, as this may constitute an undesirable phenomenon in collective behavior. We divide our study into two parts. In the first one, we basically study the threshold model supposing a fixed complete network, where every one is connected to every one, like in the seminal work of Granovetter. We study the case of a uniform distribution of the threshold, of a Gaussian distribution, and finally give a result for arbitrary distributions, supposing there is one type of anti-conformist. In a second part, we suppose that the neighborhood of an agent is random, drawn at each time step from a distribution. We distinguish the case where the degree (number of links) of an agent is fixed, and where there is an arbitrary degree distribution. We show the existence of cascades and that for most societies, the opinion converges to a chaotic situation.

result.paraphrase: We present a detailed analysis of the threshold model in which conformist and anti-conformist agents coexist. Our focus is on convergence in the agents’ opinion dynamics—namely, identifying absorbing classes, cycles, and related behavior—and on whether cascade effects can arise, since these may be undesirable in collective behavior. The study is split into two parts. First, we examine the threshold model on a fixed complete network, where everyone is connected to everyone else, in the spirit of Granovetter’s seminal work. We consider a uniform threshold distribution, a Gaussian distribution, and then obtain a result for arbitrary distributions assuming a single type of anti-conformist. Second, we assume that an agent’s neighborhood is random and sampled at each time step from a distribution. In this setting, we distinguish between fixed degree (number of links) and arbitrary degree distributions. We show that cascades can occur and that, for most societies, opinion dynamics converge to a chaotic state.
